item.title: Initialize Amazon DynamoDB Table
item.description:
Initialize a storage table on Amazon DynamoDB to store the Meta metrics of Heroes.

Step Action Technical Details
1 Access DynamoDB In the AWS Console search bar, type DynamoDB > Select Tables from the left menu > Click Create table.
2 Configure Table Name Table name: dota2_hero_metrics.
3 Configure Primary Key Partition key: Enter hero_id and select data type String (S). Sort key: Enter match_date and select data type String (S).
4 Configure Settings Under Table settings, check Customize settings to optimize costs.
5 Optimize Capacity Mode Under Read/write capacity mode, select On-demand (Pay-per-request).
6 Complete Scroll to the bottom and click the orange Create table button.

item.title: Update IAM Role for AWS Glue
item.description:
In Chapter 2, the AWS Glue IAM Role was only granted permissions to work with S3. Now, because the Glue Job needs to write data directly to DynamoDB, you need to grant it these additional permissions.

Step Action Technical Details
1 Access IAM Role Open the IAM service > Select Roles > Find and click the Glue_Dota2_Processing_Role you created earlier.
2 Add Permissions In the Permissions tab, click the Add permissions button > Select Create inline policy.
3 Configure JSON Switch to the JSON tab and paste the DynamoDB write permissions code below. (Remember to replace YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID with your AWS account ID).
4 Name the Policy Click Next. Set the Policy name to: DynamoDB_Write_Dota2_Metrics.
5 Complete Click Create policy to apply the new permissions to AWS Glue.

item.title: Upgrade Glue Job: Calculate & Load Metrics
item.description:
We proceed to upgrade the PySpark source code of the AWS Glue Job. In addition to saving Parquet files to S3, Glue will directly calculate the Winrate and Pickrate, and use the boto3 library to push the results directly into DynamoDB.

Step Action Technical Details
1 Open Glue Studio In the AWS Console > Find AWS Glue > Under ETL Jobs > Open the source code of the dota2_etl_job created in section 2.3.
2 Update Script Select the Script tab, clear the old code, and replace it with the upgraded PySpark code below.
3 Configure Parameters Ensure the RAW_PATH, PROCESSED_PATH, and DynamoDB table name variables match your system.
4 Save and Run Click Save > Click Run to launch the aggregated metrics pipeline.
5 Verify Results Go to DynamoDB Console > Under Tables > Click the dota2_hero_metrics table > Click Explore table items to verify that Hero metrics records have been successfully loaded.
